summary.text: Crystal D. Peoples-Stokes has represented Buffalo's 141st Assembly District since 2003 and became Majority Leader of the New York State Assembly in December 2018.
Her official biography highlights her sponsorship of the Marijuana Regulation and Taxation Act, which passed in March 2021.

paragraphs.text: Peoples-Stokes was born and raised in Buffalo, the daughter of a school teacher and a sanitation worker, and attended Buffalo Public Schools, according to her Assembly biography.
She earned a bachelor's degree in elementary education and a master's degree in student personnel administration from Buffalo State College, and holds an honorary doctorate from Medaille College.

After working briefly as a school teacher and for the Buffalo Urban League and Citizen Action of New York, she served on the Erie County Legislature from 1993 to 2002, becoming Majority Leader in 1998.

In the Assembly she chaired a Subcommittee on Minority and Women Owned Businesses beginning in 2012 and the Committee on Governmental Operations beginning in 2015, and in June 2017 she was voted chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Legislative Women's Caucus.

Her biography says that in June 2019 she passed a law decriminalizing possession and allowing expungement of minor marijuana convictions, and in March 2021 she passed the Marijuana Regulation and Taxation Act, a bill she had sponsored for eight years.
She is a member of True Bethel Baptist Church and St. Luke's AME Zion Church and lives in Buffalo.
